en: Title: *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* (and other names) Published: Meisezahl, from the Reiunji manuscript; published in *Dhīḥ* 38 (2004), pp. 157–169 (not seen by me). Input: Klaus Wille
Oṃ, homage to the glorious Lokanātha! Homage to the Blessed One, Amoghapāśa!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, in the abode of the noble Avalokiteśvara, which was adorned with many *śāla*, *tāla*, *tamāla*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, and *atimuktaka* trees, as well as various jewel-trees. He was accompanied by a great community of monks consisting of eighteen thousand monks, and surrounded and honored by nine hundred and ninety billion *koṭi-niyuta-śata-sahasra*s of bodhisattvas, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sons of gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa heaven. Addressing the sons of gods of the class of Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Brahmakāyika, he was teaching the Dharma.

Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and knelt with his right knee upon the ground. Bowing toward the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence, he spoke these words to the Blessed One with a smiling countenance: “Blessed One, I possess a heart-mantra named Amoghapāśarāja, which I previously received in the presence of the Tathāgata Lokendrarāja, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, in the world-system Ekanavatikalpavilokitā. By means of this, Blessed One, I have inspired many hundreds of thousands of devaputras—headed by the devaputras Īśvara and Maheśvara, and led by the devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa realm—to attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Furthermore, I have attained one million meditative absorptions (samādhis), foremost among them the *asaṃmohajñānavyūha*. Moreover, Blessed One, in whatever place on earth this Amoghapāśahṛdaya circulates, it should be known, Blessed One, that in that region twelve hundred thousand devaputras, headed by the devaputras Īśvara, Maheśvara, and those of the Brahmakāyika realm, will remain for the sake of protection, shelter, and defense. Blessed One, that place on earth where this Amoghapāśahṛdaya circulates shall be regarded as a shrine (caitya). Those beings, Blessed One, who hear this Amoghapāśahṛdaya will have planted roots of merit under hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas. Blessed One, should anyone be a perpetrator of evil, a locus of all sins, one who practices sinful ways, a slanderer of the noble ones, a rejecter of the True Dharma, one destined for the Avīci hell, and a rejecter of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas—if such a person should feel remorse and take a vow of restraint for the future, [this mantra shall protect them].”

Blessed One, by the mere fasting and recitation of this very [mantra], in this very life that karma is purified, it goes to complete exhaustion, and it is turned back. Whether it be a fever lasting one day, two days, three days, or four days, or likewise a fever lasting seven days; whether it be pain in the eyes, teeth, ears, nose, lips, tongue, palate, heart, belly, sides, hips, limbs, or minor members; or pain from hemorrhoids, dysentery, diarrhea, or pain in the hands and feet; or headache; or afflictions such as *balāhaka*, *citra-kuṣṭha*, *vicarcikā*, *kiṭibha*, fistula-in-ano, *lohaliṅga*, throat-seizure, boils, epilepsy, or those known as *kākhorda* spells; or by acts of killing, binding, beating, threatening, or possession by spirits; in short, Blessed One, whether by bodily affliction, mental affliction, or seeing bad dreams, that karma goes to complete exhaustion; it goes to total purification. How much more so for pure beings who are devoted with faith! If, Blessed One, the four assemblies and the four castes—even if they are like illusions—should hear this my *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, write it, cause it to be written, master it, and cause other beings to hear it, even down to beings born in the animal realm, by placing it in their ear and giving them the ear-recitation (*karṇajāpa*), and if they contemplate these mantra-words without rejection, without form, without conceptualization, without origination, without delay, without action, free from defilements, by setting the mind in equanimity, and being devoid of the five aggregates; through this yoga, the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*) should be cultivated. Then, thousands of Buddhas from the ten directions will appear before them face-to-face, and they will perform the confession of transgressions (*atyayadeśanā*). [The same applies] as far as they shall have it written in a book and place it in their home. What need is there for much, Blessed One? Even if they should hear it out of mutual rivalry, out of fear of a master, out of compliance with others, or for the sake of mockery, it should be known, Blessed One, that by the power of the noble Avalokiteśvara, that sound will fall into the hollow of their ears.

“Blessed One, it is just as if some man were to drag, insult, and grind sandalwood, camphor, saffron, or musk on a stone or the ground, and then smear it upon himself. Yet that sandalwood, camphor, saffron, or musk does not think, ‘I have been dragged and insulted by this man; I shall overstep [his] scent. On the contrary, it remains fragrant. In the same way, Blessed One, if anyone—whether by mocking, reviling, and so forth, up to treating it with deceitful words or even without any offerings—should worship this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of mine, Blessed One, for those harsh beings it will become a cause of virtue. Wherever they are reborn, there they will never be separated from the fragrance of the equipment of morality, concentration, wisdom, and merit. It makes one truly fragrant with morality. Blessed One, if any son of good family or daughter of good family, monk or nun, layman or laywoman, or any other being, having taken up the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, should observe a fast on the eighth day of the bright fortnight and recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* seven times without speaking to others, Blessed One, twenty benefits are to be expected for them in this very life. What are the twenty? Namely: diseases will not arise in his body; and diseases that have arisen, through the power of karma, will quickly be pacified. He will have smooth, pleasing, and soft limbs. He will be dear to many people. He will obtain secret wealth, and once obtained, thieves will not steal it. He cannot be burned by fire, nor carried away by water. No king can take it away even in thought. His undertakings will flourish. There will be no fear of lightning or floods. There will be no fear of wind or rain. Having consecrated ashes or water seven times with the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, one should perform a boundary-binding for the field in all directions, intermediate directions, below, and above; all calamities will be pacified. Those who steal vitality (*ojas*) will not be able to take away his vitality. He will be dear and pleasing to all beings. He will have no fear of enemies, and any fear of enemies that has arisen will quickly be pacified. He will have no fear of humans, no fear of *kākhorda* spells, no fear of *ḍākinīs*, and no intense afflictions or secondary afflictions. He will not die by fire, poison, or weapon. Wherever he is reborn, there he will never be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity. These twenty benefits are to be expected.”
% NB no fear of ḍākinīs

They shall obtain eight further qualities. What are these eight? At the time of death, the noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before them in the form of a monk; they will pass away in peace; their vision will not be deluded; they will not flail their hands; they will not flail their feet; they will not discharge excrement, urine, or vomit at the time of death; their mindfulness will be well-established; they will not die face-down; at the time of death, they will possess inexhaustible eloquence; wherever they have made a vow for a Buddha-field, there they will be reborn; and they will never be separated from spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). This should be recited three times during each of the three periods of the day. Indeed, those who desire [purity] must avoid alcohol, meat, onions, leeks, garlic, and food left over from a refuse heap. Furthermore, this Dharma discourse named "The Heart of the Unfailing Lasso" should be heard after one has ascertained the capacity and incapacity of all sentient beings; one must not practice the "teacher’s fist" (withholding knowledge). For when impurity, stinginess, and envy have departed, one becomes a Bodhisattva. Enlightenment (*bodhi*) is attained by acting for the benefit of sentient beings, and thus one enters the ranks of the Bodhisattvas. "Enlightenment" is said to be wisdom (*prajñā*) and "being" (*sattva*) is skillful means (*upāya*); these two qualities are attained precisely through acting for the benefit of sentient beings. "If you permit me, Blessed One, may I proclaim this Heart-mantra before the Tathāgata for the sake, the welfare, and the happiness of the fourfold assembly, and for others who have committed evil."

Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara: "Speak, O Pure Being, for you consider it the right time. The Tathāgata has given his approval; in the future time, in the final age, you shall perform the work of a father for those who belong to the Bodhisattva vehicle."

Then indeed, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with unblinking eyes, addressed the Blessed One: "Listen to me, Blessed One, regarding this mandala of the gateway to liberation, which is honored by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, happiness, and liberation of the great mass of beings. Homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times! Homage to the Saṅghas of Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present! Homage to those who have gone rightly! Homage to those who have practiced rightly! Homage to the Greatly Intelligent Śāradvatīputra! Homage to the assembly of Great Bodhisattvas headed by the noble Maitreya! Homage to the Blessed Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas headed by Supratiṣṭhitaśailendrarāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇasupratibhāsavinivartiteśvararāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha! Homage to the Tathāgata Supratiṣṭhitamaṇikūṭarāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaraśmyudgataśrīkūṭarāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Vipaśyin! Homage to the Tathāgata Śikhin! Homage to the Tathāgata Viśvabhū! Homage to the Tathāgata Krakucchanda! Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakamuni! Homage to the Tathāgata Kāśyapa! Homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha! It is as follows: *Taḍyathā:* [The mantra follows]

Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā / Oṃ śame śame mahāśame rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvapāpa-praśamane svāhā / Homage to the Tathāgata Suparikīrtitanāmadheya! Homage to the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī! Homage to the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajaśrī! Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnaprabhāseśvararāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Apratihatabhaiṣajyarāja! Homage to the Tathāgata Vikrāntagāmin! Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṃgha! Homage to the Blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present! It is as follows:

Increaser of mindfulness, increaser of intelligence, increaser of progress, increaser of fortitude, increaser of wisdom, increaser of eloquence, increaser of meditation, increaser of concentration, increaser of tranquility (*śamatha*), increaser of insight (*vipaśyanā*); increaser of all factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣadharma*), for the fulfillment of all Buddha-qualities, *svāhā*. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One! Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Great Compassionate One! Having paid homage to these, I shall now recite this Heart-mantra named Amoghapāśarāja, which was uttered from the mouth of the noble Avalokiteśvara and spoken in the presence of the Tathāgata in the midst of a great assembly. May my mantra-words be effective; may there be protection for me and for all sentient beings from all fears. It is as follows: *tadyathā*... [mantra follows] ...*svāhā*.

Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu mara mara miri miri muru muru Mahākāruṇika! Sara sara siri siri suru suru curu curu ciri ciri viri viri miri miri Mahāpadmahasta! Kala kala kili kili kulu kulu Mahāśuddhasattva! Buddhya buddhya bodha bodha bodhi bodhi bodhaya bodhaya kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu Paramaśuddhasattva! Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru Mahāsthāmaprāpta! Cala cala saṃcala saṃcala vicala vicala pracala pracala eṭaṭa eṭaṭa bhara bhara bhiri bhiri bhuru bhuru tara tara tiri tiri turu turu ehy ehi Mahākāruṇika! Mahāpaśupativeśadhara!
% NB Epithet! and the others!

Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara para para vara vara mara mara lara lara hara hara hāhā hīhī hūhū, O you who wear the garment of the *Oṃkāra-Brahman*! Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara nara nara vara vara hara hara, O you whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of rays of light! Jvala jvala tapa tapa bhāsa bhāsa bhrama bhrama, O Blessed One, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods and ṛṣis—Soma, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Indra, Vāyu, Agni, and Dhanada! Suru suru curu curu muru muru dhuru dhuru, O you who assume many various forms as Sanatkumāra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, Dhanada, Vāyu, Agni, the leader of the ṛṣis, and Vināyaka! Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara, O Giver of Boons! O Avalokiteśvara, Lord of the World, who gazes upon all beings from every side; Great Lord, Lord of the Three Worlds, adorned with all virtues! Muhu muhu muru muru muya muya muñca muñca, protect, protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, all calamities, all misfortunes, all seizing spirits, all diseases, and all poisons, and from all fevers! Likewise, bind, bind [them], O deliverer from bondage, beating, threats, kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons! Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara ciri ciri curu curu, O illuminator of the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the Four Noble Truths! Tapa tapa tama tama dama dama śama śama masa masa dhama dhama, O Great Compassionate One, O dispeller of the great darkness of ignorance, O fulfiller of the six perfections! Mala mala mili mili mulu mulu ṭaṭa ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu, O you who have girded yourself with a fawn-skin, come, come, O Great Compassionate One! O shatterer of the hosts of Īśvara, Maheśvara, and the great spirits! Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru para para hara hara vara vara sara sara mara mara kara kara kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi kiṭi kuṭu kuṭu maṭa maṭa, O dweller in the realm of great purity, O Great Compassionate One! O you who wear a white sacred thread and a garland of jewel crowns, who have placed a crown of matted locks upon the head of the Omniscient One, whose palms are adorned with most wonderful lotuses, who are unshakable in meditation, concentration, and liberation, who protect the continuums of many beings, O Great Compassionate One, purifier of all karmic obscurations, fulfiller of omniscient wisdom, deliverer from all diseases, fulfiller of the hopes of all beings, bringer of comfort to all beings, homage be to you, svāhā! To the Unfailing One, svāhā! To the Unfailing Lasso, svāhā! To the Unconquered One, svāhā! To the Invincible One, svāhā! To Amitābha, svāhā! To the Son of Amitābha, svāhā! To the Crusher of Māra’s Army, svāhā! To Fearlessness and the Giver of Fearlessness, svāhā! To Victory, svāhā! To Triumph, svāhā! To Victory and Triumph, svāhā! To the Giver of Boons, svāhā! To the Bestower of Boons, svāhā! To the Pacifier of Untimely Death, svāhā! Perform this rite for me, homage be to you, svāhā! Oṃ raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ jaya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ jra jiṃ juṃ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ hūṃ jaya svāhā! Oṃ hrīḥ, O Conqueror of the Three Worlds, Unfailing Lasso, Unassailable, hrīḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ vasumati svāhā! Oṃ ārolik svāhā! Oṃ bahule bahule svāhā! Oṃ ārolik hrīḥ hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! O Blessed One, bring about the complete destruction, without remainder, of my non-virtuous karma that is to be experienced whether in this life or in the future; svāhā! To the Lotus-Handed One, svāhā! Oṃ buddhadharmasaṃghāya svāhā!

The ritual applications of this mantra, which is perfected through recitation, are as follows: (AphSū 168) By reciting it at the three times of day, one purifies the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) and brings about the purification of all karmic obstructions. With *agaru* incense, one performs the binding of boundaries (*sīmābandha*). With ashes, water, mustard seeds, stakes of *khadira* wood, and so forth, a thread should be tied for all types of fever. For all diseases, clarified butter, oil, or water should be given after having been consecrated with the mantra. For the destruction of sorcery (*kākhorda*), a weapon [is used], and a protective thread is tied. For abdominal pain, salt-water; for the neutralization of poison, earth or water. For eye disease, a white thread should be tied to the ear. For toothache, a *karavīra* tooth-stick is used. For the binding of boundaries, a five-colored thread should be consecrated twenty-one times, tied to four *khadira* stakes, and buried in the four directions; thus there will be a binding of boundaries. This applies to all protective threads, whether with water or ashes. For all planetary seizures (*graha*), a five-colored thread is used. For all fevers, a white thread. For snake bites, insect stings, scabies, *lohaliṅga*, and throat-seizures, honey and *pippalī* are used. For eye disease, fragrant water, *palāśa* water, or licorice (*madhuyaṣṭī*) water is used. For all quarrels, strife, disputes, and false accusations, one should wash the face with water that has been consecrated. In cases of trouble in another territory, kingdom, or nation, one should place a full jar, and being pure and dressed in clean garments, having performed a great worship, the mantra should be recited; a great peace (*mahāśānti*) will ensue. One should sprinkle that water, and protection is thereby established for all beings. All calamities and misfortunes are pacified. Having consecrated a sandalwood mark (*tilaka*) on the heart twenty-one times, it should be applied; all deeds of immediate retribution go to destruction. By constant recitation, there is protection of the home. By a lotus-homa, there is protection of all beings. By a sandalwood-homa, there is protection against all planets, spirits (*bhūta*), and constellations. [The following herbs are used: *jayā*, *vijayā*, *aparājitā*, *nākulī*, *gandhanākūlī*, *dhāraṇī*, *abhayapāṇi*, *indriyapāṇi*, *gandhapriyaṅgu*, *tagara*, *cakrā*, *mahācakrā*, *vikrāntā*, *somarājī*, and *sunandā*. Having consecrated these according to their availability one hundred and eight times, they should be made into an amulet and worn on the head or the arm. When worn around the neck of children or at the waist of women, it produces supreme good fortune. (AphSū 169) It pacifies misfortune and grants sons. When this amulet is bound, all protection is established. Poison and fire do not affect one, and no poison-induced affliction arises. Even if one has arisen, it will not cause suffering and will be quickly pacified. It will pacify the seizing spirits (*graha*). The paralyzing of wind, clouds, and lightning is done with water or with a *karavīra* creeper, which performs all rites. The Heart-mantra of Noble Avalokiteśvara is supremely effective; even if not specifically empowered, it performs these rites.

Then, desiring to accomplish [the rite], one should have the image of the Buddha painted on a cloth using all the colors; [and] Āryāvalokiteśvara, wearing a crown of matted hair, clad in a lower garment of deerskin, assuming the attire of Paśupati, and adorned with all ornaments, should be painted by an artist who observes the *poṣadha* vows.

Then, the practitioner, having prepared a mandala before it using fallen cow dung and scattering white flowers upon it, should place eight jars filled with scented water. He should arrange eight offerings and sixty-four ritual implements. While burning agalloch incense, he should recite the vidyā-mantra eight thousand times, provided he has fasted for one day and night, or three nights, or has subsisted on the "three whites" (milk, curd, ghee), bathed at the three times of day, and is clothed in pure garments. Then, he sees himself and the image depicted before him; seeing this, he rejoices until Āryāvalokiteśvara himself arrives. He fulfills all hopes.

Having consecrated realgar and collyrium with mantras and applied it to the eyes, one then becomes invisible; one traverses the sky and attains the samādhi named *asaṃmohajñānavyūha* (the array of non-deluded knowledge). Whatever the practitioner desires, that very thing he accomplishes.
(Note: This refers to invisibility and the power of flight.)

The Blessed One said this, and the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, those monks, those Bodhisattvas, the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
Thus ends the Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled *The Great Heart of the Unfailing Lasso*.
